report.incidentSummary: On 2026-09-30 starting at 11:07 IST (05:37 UTC), KYC submissions began failing with HTTP 500 errors for users submitting applications with residency type 'NRI_OCI'. The error rate jumped from ~0.34% to ~9.4%. The failure was caused by deployment CHG-48220 (v1.16.0) of kyc-service, deployed at 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC). A timestamp timezone omission by legacy-jenkins-mum caused the change store to record the deploy time as 11:05 UTC (16:35 IST), leading on-call engineers to falsely rule out the deployment and suspect upstream KYC agency slowness.
report.rootCauseStatement: Deployment CHG-48220 (kyc-service v1.16.0), completed at 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC), introduced support for NRI/OCI residency types in KYC submission but failed to handle 'NRI_OCI' in the internal payload serialization schema. As a result, serialization fails with 'unknown enum value NRI_OCI for field residency_type', causing HTTP 500 errors on ~9.4% of KYC submissions.

hypotheses.cause: Deployment CHG-48220 (v1.16.0) introduced an unhandled enum value 'NRI_OCI' for field residency_type in kyc-service serialization logic, causing HTTP 500 errors.
hypotheses.rationale: Logs immediately following the deployment of v1.16.0 at 05:35 UTC show 794 occurrences of serialization error 'unknown enum value NRI_OCI for field residency_type', perfectly matching the 9.4% error rate jump starting at 05:37 UTC.

hypotheses.cause: Upstream KYC agency degradation or timeout caused KYC submissions to fail.
hypotheses.rationale: While kyc-service logged benign slow-call warnings (2.8s-3.8s) uniformly across the window, agency latency p95 remained stable at ~1.78s with no timeout or connection errors. Submission errors were 100% internal HTTP 500 serialization failures inside kyc-service before or during request dispatch.

facts.statement: kyc-service error rate rose from ~0.34% at 05:30 UTC to 2.16% at 05:35 UTC, and stabilized at ~9.4% from 05:40 UTC through 11:45 UTC.

Starting at 05:37:00.962 UTC (11:07 IST), kyc-service emitted 794 HTTP 500 error logs with message 'KYC <ref> submit failed: serialization error: unknown enum value NRI_OCI for field residency_type' on version 1.16.0.
CHG-48220 deployed kyc-service version 1.15.3 -> 1.16.0 ('release: NRI/OCI residency types in KYC submission') via deployer legacy-jenkins-mum with timestamp 2026-09-30T11:05:00.000 and tz 'none'.
kyc-service agency_latency_p95_ms remained stable between 1639 ms and 1894 ms across the entire 05:00 to 11:45 UTC window.
Database active connections (~167 avg) and message queue consumer lag (~1.96s avg) remained normal throughout the window.

inferences.statement: The deployer legacy-jenkins-mum runs in Mumbai (IST, UTC+05:30) and emitted local time 11:05 IST without offset, which corresponds to 05:35 UTC (2 minutes before failure onset at 05:37 UTC). The change store indexed it as UTC, leading on-call engineers to falsely calculate a deploy time of 16:35 IST.
The ~9.4% error rate on kyc-service accounts specifically for users submitting KYC applications with the new residency type 'NRI_OCI', which the serialization module rejects.

assumptions.statement: The pipeline build-59012 in legacy-jenkins-mum writes timestamps in local server time (IST) rather than standard ISO-8601 UTC.

timeline.event: kyc-service running v1.15.3 at baseline error rate ~0.34%. Routine slow-response warnings to kyc-agency observed with no failures.
kyc-service v1.16.0 deployed under CHG-48220 via legacy-jenkins-mum (recorded as 11:05:00 tz: none).
First HTTP 500 error logged on kyc-service v1.16.0 for unknown enum value 'NRI_OCI'.
kyc-service error rate jumps to ~9.4% and remains sustained.
Incident INC-5216 opened by On-call SRE suspecting kyc-agency after misinterpreting the release time as 16:35 IST.

confidence.rationale: Exact error signature in logs directly names the 'NRI_OCI' enum value introduced by deployment CHG-48220, coinciding directly with the deployment time once corrected from local IST to UTC.

gaps.description: Source code diff of kyc-service v1.16.0 was not directly inspected.
gaps.impact: Minimal; the log message explicitly identifies the serialization enum validation failure on 'NRI_OCI'.

recommendedActions.action: Roll back kyc-service to version 1.15.3 immediately or deploy a hotfix that includes 'NRI_OCI' in the residency_type serialization schema/enum.
recommendedActions.rationale: Removes the unhandled enum serialization failure and restores KYC submission functionality for NRI/OCI users.
recommendedActions.verification: Check kyc-service error_rate returns to baseline (~0.35%) and no further 'serialization error: unknown enum value NRI_OCI' logs appear.

recommendedActions.action: Update legacy-jenkins-mum build pipelines to emit explicit UTC ISO-8601 timestamps with timezone offsets when logging deployments to the change store.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents timezone misinterpretations in the change audit system that caused on-call engineers to falsely dismiss the deployment.
recommendedActions.verification: Trigger a staging release from legacy-jenkins-mum and confirm the change store records timestamps with explicit +00:00 or +05:30 offsets.

recommendedActions.action: Add end-to-end integration tests and schema validation tests in kyc-service CI pipelines covering all allowed enum variants for residency_type.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents mismatches between API request models and internal serialization schemas before code reaches production.
recommendedActions.verification: Run CI pipeline with a test case submitting residency_type='NRI_OCI' and ensure serialization succeeds.

findings.summary: Investigation into changes across kyc-service, api-gateway, and database on 2026-09-30 revealed a critical deployment timeline discrepancy. kyc-service was deployed with v1.16.0 (CHG-48220, 'release: NRI/OCI residency types in KYC submission') via legacy-jenkins-mum with local timestamp 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC), just 2 minutes before the failure onset at 11:07 IST (05:37 UTC). The reporter's belief that the release occurred at 16:35 IST was caused by the change store indexing the timezone-less timestamp (11:05) as UTC. No other deployments or config updates occurred on database or api-gateway. Past incident PIR-1205 involved kyc-agency scheduled maintenance resulting in pending backlog rather than submission failures, making release CHG-48220 the primary suspect.

observations.statement: A single deployment CHG-48220 was recorded for kyc-service on 2026-09-30: version 1.15.3 -> 1.16.0 ('release: NRI/OCI residency types in KYC submission') by deploy-bot via pipeline build-59012 on deployer legacy-jenkins-mum. The recorded timestamp was 2026-09-30T11:05:00.000 with tz: 'none'. No configuration changes, infrastructure updates, or deployments were recorded for api-gateway or database in the window 2026-09-30T00:00:00.000Z to 2026-09-30T11:45:00.000Z.

The deployer legacy-jenkins-mum runs in Mumbai (IST, UTC+05:30) and emitted a local timestamp without a timezone offset (11:05:00 IST = 05:35:00 UTC). The change store indexed it as UTC without offset conversion, leading the reporter to calculate 11:05 UTC + 05:30 = 16:35 IST and mistakenly dismiss the release. In reality, deployment CHG-48220 completed at approximately 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC), exactly 2 minutes prior to the incident onset at 11:07 IST (05:37 UTC).

kyc-service sits downstream of api-gateway (sync, timeout 3000ms, retries 0) and receives webhooks from kyc-agency. Downstream, kyc-service depends on database (datastore, timeout 1000ms, retries 0), kyc-agency (external_api, timeout 5000ms, retries 1), and message-queue (async).

Past incident PIR-1205 (2026-09-17, SEV3) was titled 'KYC applications on hold after agency maintenance'. Its root cause was scheduled maintenance on kyc-agency causing pending KYC counts to accumulate by ~900 until afternoon resumption.

Unlike PIR-1205 where requests were held pending due to external agency maintenance, current symptoms are active submission failures for some users starting immediately after CHG-48220 (v1.16.0), which introduced NRI/OCI residency types in KYC submissions.

# Investigation report: KYC submissions failing

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** critic_accepted · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
On 2026-09-30 starting at 11:07 IST (05:37 UTC), KYC submissions began failing with HTTP 500 errors for users submitting applications with residency type 'NRI_OCI'. The error rate jumped from ~0.34% to ~9.4%. The failure was caused by deployment CHG-48220 (v1.16.0) of kyc-service, deployed at 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC). A timestamp timezone omission by legacy-jenkins-mum caused the change store to record the deploy time as 11:05 UTC (16:35 IST), leading on-call engineers to falsely rule out the deployment and suspect upstream KYC agency slowness.

**Root cause:** Deployment CHG-48220 (kyc-service v1.16.0), completed at 11:05 IST (05:35 UTC), introduced support for NRI/OCI residency types in KYC submission but failed to handle 'NRI_OCI' in the internal payload serialization schema. As a result, serialization fails with 'unknown enum value NRI_OCI for field residency_type', causing HTTP 500 errors on ~9.4% of KYC submissions.

## Hypotheses
1. **Deployment CHG-48220 (v1.16.0) introduced an unhandled enum value 'NRI_OCI' for field residency_type in kyc-service serialization logic, causing HTTP 500 errors.** — `kyc-service`, deployment_regression, confidence 0.95, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_2, ev_8, ev_10, ev_11, ev_12, ev_14, ev_15] · Contradicting: none
   - Logs immediately following the deployment of v1.16.0 at 05:35 UTC show 794 occurrences of serialization error 'unknown enum value NRI_OCI for field residency_type', perfectly matching the 9.4% error rate jump starting at 05:37 UTC.
2. **Upstream KYC agency degradation or timeout caused KYC submissions to fail.** — `kyc-agency`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_11, ev_13] · Contradicting: [ev_3, ev_5, ev_6, ev_10, ev_12]
   - While kyc-service logged benign slow-call warnings (2.8s-3.8s) uniformly across the window, agency latency p95 remained stable at ~1.78s with no timeout or connection errors. Submission errors were 100% internal HTTP 500 serialization failures inside kyc-service before or during request dispatch.

## Facts
- kyc-service error rate rose from ~0.34% at 05:30 UTC to 2.16% at 05:35 UTC, and stabilized at ~9.4% from 05:40 UTC through 11:45 UTC. [ev_2]
- Starting at 05:37:00.962 UTC (11:07 IST), kyc-service emitted 794 HTTP 500 error logs with message 'KYC <ref> submit failed: serialization error: unknown enum value NRI_OCI for field residency_type' on version 1.16.0. [ev_10, ev_11, ev_12, ev_15]
- CHG-48220 deployed kyc-service version 1.15.3 -> 1.16.0 ('release: NRI/OCI residency types in KYC submission') via deployer legacy-jenkins-mum with timestamp 2026-09-30T11:05:00.000 and tz 'none'. [ev_8, ev_14]
- kyc-service agency_latency_p95_ms remained stable between 1639 ms and 1894 ms across the entire 05:00 to 11:45 UTC window. [ev_3, ev_5]
- Database active connections (~167 avg) and message queue consumer lag (~1.96s avg) remained normal throughout the window. [ev_4, ev_9]

## Inferences
- The deployer legacy-jenkins-mum runs in Mumbai (IST, UTC+05:30) and emitted local time 11:05 IST without offset, which corresponds to 05:35 UTC (2 minutes before failure onset at 05:37 UTC). The change store indexed it as UTC, leading on-call engineers to falsely calculate a deploy time of 16:35 IST. [ev_8, ev_12, ev_14, ev_15]
- The ~9.4% error rate on kyc-service accounts specifically for users submitting KYC applications with the new residency type 'NRI_OCI', which the serialization module rejects. [ev_2, ev_10, ev_11, ev_15]

## Assumptions
- The pipeline build-59012 in legacy-jenkins-mum writes timestamps in local server time (IST) rather than standard ISO-8601 UTC.

## Timeline
- **2026-09-30T05:00:00.000Z (10:30 IST)** kyc-service running v1.15.3 at baseline error rate ~0.34%. Routine slow-response warnings to kyc-agency observed with no failures. [ev_2, ev_11, ev_13]
- **2026-09-30T05:35:00.000Z (11:05 IST)** kyc-service v1.16.0 deployed under CHG-48220 via legacy-jenkins-mum (recorded as 11:05:00 tz: none). [ev_8, ev_14]
- **2026-09-30T05:37:00.962Z (11:07:00 IST)** First HTTP 500 error logged on kyc-service v1.16.0 for unknown enum value 'NRI_OCI'. [ev_10, ev_12, ev_15]
- **2026-09-30T05:40:00.000Z (11:10 IST)** kyc-service error rate jumps to ~9.4% and remains sustained. [ev_2]
- **2026-09-30T11:35:00.000Z (17:05 IST)** Incident INC-5216 opened by On-call SRE suspecting kyc-agency after misinterpreting the release time as 16:35 IST. [ev_8, ev_14]

## Confidence
0.95: Exact error signature in logs directly names the 'NRI_OCI' enum value introduced by deployment CHG-48220, coinciding directly with the deployment time once corrected from local IST to UTC.

## Gaps
- Source code diff of kyc-service v1.16.0 was not directly inspected. (impact: Minimal; the log message explicitly identifies the serialization enum validation failure on 'NRI_OCI'.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Roll back kyc-service to version 1.15.3 immediately or deploy a hotfix that includes 'NRI_OCI' in the residency_type serialization schema/enum. [ev_2, ev_10, ev_12]
  - Why: Removes the unhandled enum serialization failure and restores KYC submission functionality for NRI/OCI users.
  - Verify: Check kyc-service error_rate returns to baseline (~0.35%) and no further 'serialization error: unknown enum value NRI_OCI' logs appear.
- **[next]** Update legacy-jenkins-mum build pipelines to emit explicit UTC ISO-8601 timestamps with timezone offsets when logging deployments to the change store. [ev_8, ev_14]
  - Why: Prevents timezone misinterpretations in the change audit system that caused on-call engineers to falsely dismiss the deployment.
  - Verify: Trigger a staging release from legacy-jenkins-mum and confirm the change store records timestamps with explicit +00:00 or +05:30 offsets.
- **[later]** Add end-to-end integration tests and schema validation tests in kyc-service CI pipelines covering all allowed enum variants for residency_type. [ev_8, ev_15]
  - Why: Prevents mismatches between API request models and internal serialization schemas before code reaches production.
  - Verify: Run CI pipeline with a test case submitting residency_type='NRI_OCI' and ensure serialization succeeds.
